steps: Cut a few slits in the brinjal, push a garlic clove into some of them and rub the skin with a little of the oil.
Roast it right on a gas flame on medium-high for 10 to 12 minutes, turning often, until black all over and a knife slides in easily.
Let it cool for about 10 minutes, then peel off the skin and mash the flesh with the roasted garlic.
Heat the rest of the oil in a pan on medium, let the cumin sizzle, then fry the chopped ginger, garlic and green chilli for about 2 minutes.
Add the chopped onion and cook on medium for 2 to 3 minutes, until soft but not brown.
Stir in the chilli powder and coriander powder, add the tomato and cook for about 5 minutes, until it turns mushy.
Mix in the mashed brinjal and the salt and cook on low for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring often.
Turn off the heat, stir in the garam masala and coriander leaves, and serve hot with roti.
note: The sources disagree a lot on eggplant: one uses 100 g a person, the other about 275 g. 200 g of raw eggplant was kept as a fair middle, since it shrinks a lot once roasted and peeled; garlic comes down from 8.5 g to 5 g.
